A child who is 3 months old with frequent crying, especially at night, along with breathing difficulties and coughing, most likely has **colic** — a common condition in young infants caused by trapped gas in the intestines.

The nighttime coughing and breathing difficulties are simply because when babies lie flat at night, the gas pressure increases, making them uncomfortable and causing them to cry and breathe harder.

You should give the baby **gripe water or simethicone drops** (gas relief medication) regularly, as this will relieve the trapped gas and stop the coughing and breathing difficulties.

The mother should also avoid eating certain foods like beans, cabbage, and dairy products while breastfeeding, as these foods pass through breast milk and cause more gas in the baby.

This condition resolves completely on its own by **4-6 months of age**, so there is nothing serious to worry about, and no further medical tests are needed.

The oxygen given at birth quickly reverses any temporary lack of breathing, and since the resuscitation was done promptly, the brain and other organs would have received adequate oxygen supply throughout. Babies who are resuscitated at birth rarely develop any neurological problems, as the brain is very resilient in newborns. The fact that the baby started breathing well after oxygen was given is an excellent sign that full recovery is expected. This baby should develop normally like any other child with no need for special follow-up care.
